idiom_name: CASL MongoAbility typed over Actions/Subjects with an ability.can() check in a NestJS CanActivate guard (nest-casl @UseAbility) or node-casbin enforcer
implementation_notes: TypeScript inherits CASL from JavaScript and adds types: declare type Actions and type Subjects, instantiate MongoAbility<[Actions, Subjects]>, and build it per request from the authenticated user's roles with AbilityBuilder - if (user.roles.includes('editor')) can('update', 'Article', { authorId: user.id }). The ability.can(action, subject) call is the decision; in a NestJS API the enforcement seam is a guard, either the documented hand-written CanActivate + Reflector pattern that reads required permissions from @Permissions/@RequirePermissions metadata (registered as APP_GUARD so new endpoints are covered) or the nest-casl integration, whose @UseAbility(action, subject) decorator with AccessGuard performs the same check using lazy subject hooks (SubjectBeforeFilterHook) for condition-based rules and an AccessService for programmatic checks. For table-style policy node-casbin provides Enforce(sub, obj, act) from model.conf/policy.csv. Types describe the vocabulary; they do not enforce it at runtime, so the guard must still check and deny by default.
pitfalls: The Actions/Subjects types are compile-time only; a value from a request cast to the type passes the compiler but not the ability, so the guard's runtime can() check is what matters.
A guard applied per route is forgotten on new endpoints; register it as APP_GUARD and deny when the required-permission metadata is absent.
Roles read from the JWT or a client payload are claims, not permissions; rebuild the ability server-side from the role store so a stale or forged role cannot widen access.
Checking ability.can(action, 'Article') without the instance skips conditions, silently ignoring an ownership rule; pass the loaded subject for object-level decisions.
Rebuilding the ability per request is correct but must read current role data; caching it across a revocation serves a removed role until the cache expires.
